doc.title: Melba Liston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Little Niles, 1956 version
summary: They hear her 1956 arrangement of Randy Weston's Little Niles, featuring bass, with a Monk flavor.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: In less than in two years. Coming up right now, we’re going to do one of Randy Weston’s tunes, a song that was recorded for the first time I think in 1956. It’s called Little Niles, and it’s Melba Liston’s arrangement of it, and this is another one of the styles and different ways that Melba writes. We want to hear this. Little Niles. [The music plays.] I like the way the bass comes in.
Yeah, that was featuring the bass.
And the – it had a flavor of . . .
I don’t get to hear Randy’s work that often. That a 1956 version of that.
Yeah. You want to go on and hear [?] or this one – the strings?
Oh yeah, because I haven’t heard you do strings arrangement.
Or else I can do the one that I’m featured on.
Yeah. You said that was next.
Can you cue that up for us? But you were on this one too.
Yeah, but I didn’t know. I forgot. The other one is more ballad and it’s easier.
